$comment: Per-topic grades for site/quaestiones.json: whether a reader arriving with the topic's own
`question` leaves with it answered by the anchored passages. The METHOD, the scale and every
general finding are in docs/research/topic-anchor-review.md; only the rows live here, so a
grade has one copy.
WHY JSON RATHER THAN THE TABLE IT REPLACED: a grade is a claim about a particular anchor set,
and anchor sets change. `anchors` states the set that was graded, quaestiones.test.ts
recomputes it from the source, and a mismatch is the one defect a markdown table could never
report -- a topic re-anchored after somebody read it, still showing the old verdict. The test
FAILS on drift and names the topic, its graded set and its current one; the fix is to re-read
the topic, not to paste the new signature in. Being made to look is the whole mechanism.
GRADES. A: the passages answer the question as asked, in their own words. B: the answer is
there but the reader has to carry it across from a passage written about an adjacent thing --
a real grade, not a soft A, and the note says what would replace it. C: something the title,
question or keywords promise has no anchored text and the corpus HAS a text -- fix it, do not
file it. D: the missing half needs a document the corpus does not have; see the blocklist in
docs/research/topics.md.
NO C OR D IS RECORDED HERE and that is by design: a C found is a C fixed in the same pass, so
`was` is where they appear. A topic that cannot be fixed is a D and belongs to the blocklist
rather than to this file.
ABSENCE IS NOT A PASS. A topic missing from `reviewed` has not been read. The pass runs a
cluster at a time and the markdown says which are outstanding.

dei-existentia.note: 31–34 is the Catechism's own version of the converging arguments, and 36–37 says God can be known with certainty by reason and then says at length why that is hard, which is the half a sceptic is owed. Was diluted: 39–43 is _How can we speak about God?_ — analogy and the limits of religious language — and a reader asking whether anyone is there has not asked it. Narrowed 2026-09-10.

malum.note: 309 opens by asking the reader's own question in the Catechism's words and refuses a quick answer; 310–312 give the one there is, and end on “evil never becomes a good”. 313 is addressed to “those who are scandalized and rebel against what happens to them”, which is who arrives here.

scandalum-cleri.note: 827 and 1550 answer why anyone should trust it after that: the Church holds sinners and is always in need of purification, and a minister's sin cannot impede the grace of the sacraments. Was C: the keywords led with _cover up_ and _bishops_ and every anchored canon was about the abuser. Fixed 2026-09-10 with can. 1378 §2 — culpable negligence in performing or omitting an act of office, with harm to another or scandal — which is the sentence for the man who did nothing. No document: the corpus has neither _Vos estis lux mundi_ nor _Sacramentorum sanctitatis tutela_.

lex-naturalis.note: The question is why anyone would need religion to be good and 1954–1959 answers that they do not: the natural law is human reason, written in every heart, binding on all men and surviving its own rejection. 1960 states the qualification in the Church's terms rather than ours, which is what keeps the page from arguing.

scriptura-inspirata.note: Was C: 105–108 answers _who wrote it_ and stops, while the keywords promised _contradictions_, _literal_, _myth_ and _historical accuracy_. The paragraphs that answer those were the next six, directly under the anchor the topic already had — 110 on literary genres and truth being “differently presented and expressed in the various types of historical writing”, 111–114 on the three criteria. Widened 2026-09-10. Stops at 114: the four senses at 115–119 are how the Church reads Scripture, not why a doubter should believe it.

canon-scripturae.note: 120 prints all 46 books and says the Church discerned them by apostolic Tradition, which answers “added or taken away” without ever putting it that way; 123 is the nearest the Catechism comes to the dispute, on refusing to reject the Old Testament. Was diluted: 124–130 is the Gospels and typology, and 126 went to `iesus-christus`, where its historicity clause is the point; narrowed 2026-09-10. B because the keywords name _trent_, _apocrypha_ and _protestant bible_ and no anchored sentence names the disagreement — the Catechism does not, and the corpus has no Tridentine decree.

creatio-et-scientia.note: 283 grants the sciences their own results and 284 says the question of meaning is “of another order”, which is the answer to whether science has settled it; 289 reads Genesis 1–3 by its literary standpoint. Was C: the keywords promised _adam and eve_ and _evolution_ and neither had an anchored sentence. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 366, the spiritual soul created immediately by God and not produced by the parents, and 390, the fall told in figurative language and affirmed as a primeval event.

iesus-christus.note: Was C, and the widest miss in this cluster: a reader asking whether any of it happened was given 422–429 on how to catechise and 456–460 on why the Word became flesh, with the Resurrection nowhere on the page. Re-anchored 2026-09-10 on 423, the claim dated by Herod, Augustus, Pilate and Tiberius; 126, the three stages of the Gospels' formation; 639–644, which dates 1 Cor 15 to about A.D. 56, says the empty tomb “in itself is not a direct proof”, and says the hypothesis that the apostles' faith produced the Resurrection will not hold up; and 647, where no one was an eyewitness to the Resurrection itself and no evangelist describes it. The last is what makes the page honest rather than only persuasive.

novissima.note: The whole of _I believe in life everlasting_, and the one place in this cluster a twenty-two paragraph span is right: “is that all there is” is answered by the particular judgment, heaven, purgatory, hell and the last judgment in that order, and a reader who stops early has stopped on an answer. 1038 carries the resurrection of the dead, which is the only keyword the article names in passing.

atheismus.note: Was C: the keywords ended on _invincible ignorance_ and _good atheists_, and the page ran from “atheism is a sin against the virtue of religion” to “agnosticism is all too often equivalent to practical atheism” with nothing after it. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 1260 — a man ignorant of the Gospel who seeks the truth and does the will of God as he understands it can be saved. 1260 and not 847, whose first clause (“this affirmation is not aimed at”) points back at a sentence that is not on this page. 2125 already carried the other half: believers can have more than a little to do with the rise of atheism.

beata-virgo.note: Was C: the keywords named _immaculate conception_, _perpetual virginity_ and _brothers of jesus_, and not one of the seventeen anchored paragraphs said any of it — 966 mentions the Immaculate Virgin in passing and that was all. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 491–492 and 499–500, the last of which opens “Against this doctrine the objection is sometimes raised that the Bible mentions brothers and sisters of Jesus” and answers it. 970 and 971 were already carrying the question itself: Marian devotion “differs essentially from the adoration” given to God. The prayer block was cut to 2676–2677, the Ave Maria taken line by line, since a reader asking why she is given so much is owed the prayer rather than its history.

sancti-et-imagines.note: 956 and 957 answer the question and 2132 answers it twice over — the honour paid to an image is “not the adoration due to God alone”. Was C on _canonisation_, a keyword with no anchored sentence; 828 was added 2026-09-10. Also diluted: 946–953 is communion in faith, sacraments, charisms and goods, ten paragraphs a reader asking about idolatry would read before reaching the intercession of the saints, and the span now opens at the Catechism’s own heading _The communion of the Church of heaven and earth_.

purgatorium.note: The question is where any of it is in the Bible, and 1031 and 1032 answer for purgatory in their own words — a cleansing fire by reference to texts of Scripture, and prayer for the dead “already mentioned in Sacred Scripture”. B because nothing in 1471–1479 does the same for indulgences: the treasury and the power of binding and loosing are stated, not sourced, and the reader has to carry Matthew 16 across from 1478. Note also that 1032’s proof text is 2 Maccabees, which is precisely the book the reader asking this question does not have — see `canon-scripturae`. Paul VI’s constitution on indulgences was added 2026-09-10; the topic had no document at all, and _tetzel_ is a keyword no anchored sentence touches. It is named against the manifest rather than against a description, which `quaestiones.json` asks for and `descriptions.json` does not have for any apostolic constitution — the only topic in the file in that state, and it is this pass's doing. Either the description gets written or the document comes back out.

primatus-romani-pontificis.note: 881 and 882 are the rock, the keys and the full, supreme and universal power, and 883–885 answer “why one man” by saying he is not alone — the college has supreme authority too, and not without its head. Was C: _infallibility_ was a keyword with no paragraph. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 890–892, which is also where the limits are: 892 is the ordinary Magisterium, taught “without arriving at an infallible definition”. Diluted at the other end: 886–887 is individual bishops, patriarchates and episcopal conferences, and was dropped. 890–892 is also on `papa-reprehensus`, which needs it for the opposite question; the sets differ.

traditio-et-scriptura.note: 82 is the sentence the question asks for: the Church “does not derive her certainty about all revealed truths from the holy Scriptures alone”, and 83 adds that the first generation of Christians did not yet have a written New Testament. Was C: _deposit of faith_ and _magisterium_ were keywords and the span stopped at 83. Widened 2026-09-10 to 86, which is the disarming half — “this Magisterium is not superior to the Word of God, but is its servant”. Stops at 86: 87 is addressed to the faithful receiving their pastors with docility, and this reader is not one of them. 84–86 is shared with `concilium-vaticanum-secundum`.

iustificatio.note: The question is whether Catholics think they earn heaven and 2007 answers it flatly — “there is no strict right to any merit on the part of man” — with 2010 and Thérèse’s empty hands at 2011 behind it. Was C on _once saved always saved_, which had no anchored sentence; 2005 was added 2026-09-10 and is the exact one: grace “cannot be known except by faith”, we cannot rely on our feelings or our works to conclude that we are saved, and Joan of Arc’s answer to the trap. No document: the corpus has no decree of Trent and no joint declaration.

confessio-sacerdoti.note: 1441 answers the question in two sentences — only God forgives sins, and he gives this power to men to exercise in his name — and the canons answer the fear behind the keywords by making the seal inviolable. Was C: _examination of conscience_ and _telling a man my sins_ were keywords with nothing behind them. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 1454–1456, where 1455 is the human argument (disclosure “frees us”) and 1456 the reason it is said aloud: “if the sick person is too ashamed to show his wound to the doctor, the medicine cannot heal what it does not know.” Shared with `scrupulositas` and `reditus`, which need those paragraphs for a reader already inside the confessional rather than outside it.

eucharistia.note: 1374–1377 answers “is it bread, or is it not” about as directly as the Catechism answers anything, transubstantiation named and defined at 1376. Was C on _last supper_: the words the whole question turns on — “This is my body which is given for you” — were on no page here. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 1338–1339, which now open it, so the reader meets the claim in Christ’s words before meeting the Church’s account of them.

unitas-christianorum.note: 817 says the rifts arose with “men of both sides to blame” and 818 says those born into those communities cannot be charged with the separation and have a right to be called Christians, which is the answer and the tone. Was C: _one true church_ and _orthodox_ were keywords with no anchored sentence. Widened 2026-09-10 to 816, the _subsistit in_ paragraph directly above the old anchor, and 838, which says of the Orthodox Churches that the communion “lacks little to attain the fullness that would permit a common celebration of the Lord’s Eucharist”.

doctrinae-progressus.note: 66 is the answer in principle — Revelation is complete and “has not been made completely explicit; it remains for Christian faith gradually to grasp its full significance over the course of the centuries” — and 94 says how that grasp grows. B because the reader asks the sharp form, and no anchored sentence says a past teaching can be corrected rather than deepened; _usury_, _slavery_ and _limbo_ are keywords the Catechism never takes up, and the three documents carry that weight alone. Was diluted: 67 is private revelations, which is `apparitiones`, and dropping it 2026-09-10 also ended the only subset pair in this doorway.

papa-reprehensus.note: Was C, and the miss was the question’s own verb: 888–892 says what is protected and what gets religious assent, and nothing anchored said a Catholic may say anything at all. Fixed 2026-09-10 with can. 212, which carries both halves in one canon — §1 the obedience owed to pastors who represent Christ, §3 the right “and even at times the duty” to manifest an opinion on matters pertaining to the good of the Church, and to make it known to the rest of the faithful — and CCC 907, the same sentence in the Catechism. The canon is the better half because the reader’s word here is a legal one.

dissensus.note: 1790 is the sentence this reader came for — “a human being must always obey the certain judgment of his conscience” — and 1791–1793 are the qualification, in the Catechism’s order and not ours. It sat ninth on the page; `lead` moves it first as of 2026-09-10. Was C on _obey the church_ and _private judgment_, which had no anchored text: 2039 now says conscience “should not be set in opposition to the moral law or the Magisterium”, and 2038 is the half that keeps it from being one-sided — the Holy Spirit “can use the humblest to enlighten the learned and those in the highest positions”.

concilium-vaticanum-secundum.note: Was answering a different question: 84–87 is the deposit and the Magisterium, and a reader asking whether the Church became something else in 1965 got four paragraphs on who interprets the Word of God. Widened 2026-09-10 with 66 (no new public revelation), 1124–1125 (“even the supreme authority in the Church may not change the liturgy arbitrarily”) and 1205–1206 (an immutable part, parts that can be changed, and diversity that “can also provoke tensions”). B because no anchored sentence names a council or a year, and the keywords _latin mass_, _tridentine_, _sspx_ and _lefebvre_ have none at all. The corpus holds both _Summorum Pontificum_ and _Traditionis Custodes_ and this pass did not name them, on the ground that `docs/research/topics.md` blocked the Latin Mass as a topic. That row was then found to have expired — it was waiting for documents the corpus had already acquired — and was removed on 2026-09-10. Naming the two is now an ordinary editorial choice and not a blocklist question, and it is still open.

synodalitas.note: 877–879 answers who decides — the ministry is collegial and personal at once — and 894–895 says the bishops’ power is “proper, ordinary, and immediate” and that they “should not be thought of as vicars of the Pope”. Was C: _synod_, _laity_ and _consultation_ were keywords with no anchored sentence. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 887, the only paragraph in the Catechism that says synods and episcopal conferences, and 907 and 910 for the laity — the right to be heard, and the call to cooperate through ministries. 887 was dropped from `primatus-romani-pontificis` in the same pass, where it was dilution and here is the answer.

mulieres-in-ecclesia.note: Was C and a door mismatch: the question is whether the Church is run by men for men, and the anchor was 369–373 on man and woman in creation — 372 is about marriage and transmitting life, addressed to a different reader entirely. Re-anchored 2026-09-10 on 369 and 370 (equal dignity, and “in no way is God in man’s image. He is neither man nor woman”, which is the answer to _patriarchy_) and on what lay people may actually do: 903 for lector and acolyte, 906 for teaching the sacred sciences, 907 for the right to be heard, 910 for ministries. B because none of those says _woman_: the Catechism has no passage on women in the Church’s governance, and the CDF letter carries it. Ordination is `ordinatio-mulierum`.

charismata.note: “Was what I felt from God” is answered by 800 and 801 in their own words — accepted with gratitude “provided they really are genuine gifts”, and “no charism is exempt from being referred and submitted to the Church’s shepherds” — with charity named as the measure. 2003 already carried _tongues_. Was C on _faith healing_; 1508 was added 2026-09-10, and it is the honest one: a special charism of healing exists, and “even the most intense prayers do not always obtain the healing of all illnesses”. Shared with `aegritudo`. No document: nothing in the corpus is addressed to the charismatic renewal.

caritas.note: Was C: the question is a couple saying they love each other, and the keywords named _eros_, _romantic_ and _feelings_, while every anchored paragraph treated charity as a theological virtue already possessed. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 1766, “to love is to will the good of another”, which is the sentence that separates love from a feeling, and 1604, love as “the fundamental and innate vocation of every human being”. 1824 was already carrying the rest — charity “keeps the commandments of God and his Christ”. Was also diluted: CSDC 207–208 is social and political charity, legislation and structures and worldwide poverty, and was dropped; 204 stays because its first sentence is this reader’s premise stated as an error — love “often restricted to relationships of physical closeness or limited to merely subjective aspects”.

contraceptio.note: 2366 gives the reason and 2370 the judgement, side by side with periodic continence, so a reader asking why it is forbidden gets the argument and the alternative in one paragraph. _Vasectomy_ and _sterilisation_ are covered by 2370’s “whether in anticipation of the conjugal act” rather than by name; the paragraph that says the word is 2399, which is on `post-contraceptionem` where the reader has already done it.

fecundatio-artificialis.note: 2374 opens where this reader is — “couples who discover that they are sterile suffer greatly” — and 2376 and 2377 give the two judgements and the reason for each, including that homologous technique is “perhaps less reprehensible, yet remain[s] morally unacceptable”. Was C on _frozen embryos_: 2275 says embryos may not be produced “intended for exploitation as disposable biological material” and was sitting on `abortus`, where it was dilution; moved 2026-09-10. That also ended the subset relation with `sterilitas`.

concubinatus.note: 2391 answers the question as asked — the “right to a trial marriage”, and why the Catechism says human love does not tolerate one — and 2390 states what a free union is and is not. Was C on _fornication_, which is a keyword and appears in exactly one paragraph: 2353, added 2026-09-10.

divortium.note: The whole of the Catechism’s _Divorce_ heading, and it earns being taken whole: 2382 is the indissolubility, 2383 concedes that civil divorce “can be tolerated” for legal rights and the care of children, and 2386 distinguishes the spouse unjustly abandoned from the one who destroyed the marriage. A reader who stops at 2384 has read the hardest sentence; the two after it are why the page must not stop there.

homosexualitas.note: The Catechism’s own heading, all three paragraphs, with 2359 answering what is asked and 2358 first. The `lead` was examined and kept: 2358’s closing sentence is itself an ask addressed to this reader — to unite to the Cross “the difficulties they may encounter from their condition” — so the disclosure that the paragraph answering directly is placed first remains true. The three documents are 1975, 1986 and 2003, and nothing on the page says so; that is PLAN.md gap 19 and not this topic’s defect.

identitas-sexualis.note: CCC 2333 — “everyone, man and woman, should acknowledge and accept his sexual identity” — is the only sentence in the Catechism that bears on the question, and 2332 is the one that says sexuality concerns the person “in the unity of his body and soul”. B because that is all there is: the article was written in 1992 and the question was not being asked of it, and _dignitas-infinita_ (2024) is the only text in the corpus that takes up gender theory and transition in its own terms — a document, so it is named and not quoted. Was diluted: 2335 is marriage and one flesh and 2336 is adultery and lust, and a reader who arrived asking what the Church says about being trans was reading neither of their questions. Narrowed 2026-09-10.

ordinatio-mulierum.note: Two paragraphs and no more is right here: 1577 answers the question in its last sentence, and 1578 supplies the thing the question assumes and the Church denies — that anyone has a right to orders at all. _Deaconess_ is a keyword with no anchored sentence and the corpus has none: 1577 covers the diaconate only as a degree of orders, and the commissions of 2016 and 2020 published nothing the corpus holds.

caelibatus.note: 1579 gives the reason and 1580 gives the reader the fact that usually surprises them, in the Catechism’s own words: in the Eastern Churches married men are ordained deacons and priests, and the practice “has long been considered legitimate”. So the page answers _why_ without pretending the discipline is universal. _Shortage of priests_ is a keyword nothing anchored takes up, and nothing in the corpus argues it either way.

abortus.note: 2270 and 2271 answer why it is treated as the gravest, and 2272 gives the excommunication with the sentence that has to go beside it — “the Church does not thereby intend to restrict the scope of mercy”; the remission is on `post-abortum`, at can. 1357. B because three keywords — _rape_, _ectopic pregnancy_, _morning after pill_ — are the hardest cases a reader arrives with and the Catechism takes up none of them; _evangelium-vitae_ is the nearest text and is already named. Was diluted: 2275 is embryo research and moved to `fecundatio-artificialis` 2026-09-10.

euthanasia.note: Four paragraphs that answer the question as asked and refuse the caricature: 2277 forbids it, 2278 permits discontinuing burdensome treatment, and 2279 permits painkillers “even at the risk of shortening their days” and calls palliative care “a special form of disinterested charity”. A reader asking why anyone is refused a death without pain is told that most of what they mean by that is already licit.

poena-capitalis.note: The one topic in the corpus whose question is about a change, and the text answers it itself: 2267 as revised in 2018 opens “was long considered an appropriate response” and closes on inadmissibility, so the reader is shown the change inside the paragraph rather than told about it. Note that CSDC 405, on `carceres`, still states the pre-2018 position and is kept there deliberately — see the open question in docs/research/topic-anchor-review.md.

castitas.note: 2348 and 2349 answer “of whom” exactly — all the baptized, in the way suited to their state of life, in three forms none of which is praised to the exclusion of the others — and 2337–2347 answer “what”. Was C on _purity_, _modesty_ and _impurity_: the whole of the Catechism’s ninth-commandment article was on no topic at all. Added 2026-09-10: 2520 on how purity is won and 2521–2522 on modesty, which “is decency” and “inspires one’s choice of clothing”. 2351 was picked up for _lust_, the only paragraph that defines it.

mendacium.note: 2484 answers the question in one sentence — a lie is venial in itself and becomes mortal when it does grave injury to justice and charity — and 2477 supplies the words the keywords promise: rash judgment, detraction, calumny. Was C on _secrets_ and _mental reservation_, which the span stopped one paragraph short of. Widened 2026-09-10 to 2489: “no one is bound to reveal the truth to someone who does not have the right to know it”, which is also the counterweight the page needed to 2485. 2488–2489 are shared with `violentia-digitalis`. No document: nothing in the corpus is addressed to truthful speech as such.

capitalismus.note: The question is answered by being refused in both directions, and the reader can see it: CSDC 176 defends private property as “an extension of human freedom” and 177 says the tradition “has never recognized the right to private property as absolute and untouchable”. Was C on _free market_, a keyword with no anchored section — the whole anchor was property and not markets. Fixed 2026-09-10 with CSDC 347–349, which appreciate the market as “the most efficient instrument for utilizing resources” and then name “the risk of an ‘idolatry’ of the market”. 179–180 were dropped as the extension to new goods and to indigenous community property; 181 stays for _greed_.

socialismus.note: 2425 answers the question in one sentence and then refuses to let it be a partisan answer: the Church “has rejected the totalitarian and atheistic ideologies associated in modern times with communism or socialism” and “has likewise refused to accept, in the practice of capitalism, individualism and the absolute primacy of the law of the marketplace”. _Liberation theology_ is a keyword with no anchored text, and the two CDF instructions that carry it are named — which is the shape this doorway is built for.

labor.note: Asked what the Church asks of an employer, 2432 answers by name — those responsible for business enterprises “have an obligation to consider the good of persons and not only the increase of profits”, with “profits are necessary, however” in the next sentence — and 2433 covers hiring without unjust discrimination. 2430 carries _unions_. The wage itself is `merces-iusta`.

migratio.note: One Catechism paragraph, and it is the whole of what the Catechism says: 2241 answers “how many” with “to the extent they are able”, then grants that authorities may make immigration subject to juridical conditions, then states the immigrant’s own duties. A reader who came for one side gets three sentences of the other. _Deportation_ and _illegal_ are keywords no anchored sentence touches; _fratelli-tutti_ is where that is.

bellum.note: Sixteen paragraphs is right here because it is two of the Catechism’s own headings and the question is the broadest in this cluster: 2309 is the criteria, 2311 conscientious objection, 2314 the indiscriminate destruction of cities, 2316 the arms trade, 2317 the injustices that cause wars. CSDC 500–501 sits here rather than on `defensio-sui`, where it was dilution about a reader defending a house.

civitas-et-oboedientia.note: The Catechism block was answering the other half of its own heading: 2234–2237 is what those in authority owe, and the question is what a citizen owes. The Compendium block was already right — CSDC 399 and 400 are the refusal and the resistance — so the page answered, but not where a reader meets it first. Widened 2026-09-10 to 2238–2240 (taxes, the vote, defence) and 2242–2243 (the limit and the five conditions for armed resistance). 2241 is skipped in the middle: it is migration, and it is `migratio`.

suffragium.note: CSDC 570 is the answer as asked — “a well-formed Christian conscience does not permit one to vote for a political programme or an individual law which contradicts the fundamental contents of faith and morals” — and 574 supplies the other half, that party membership is a personal decision legitimate within the limits of what is not incompatible with the faith. So _non-negotiable_ and _lesser evil_ both have text, which is unusual for a keyword pair this specific.

sub-imperio-atheo.note: Was C on the first half of its own question. “May a Catholic hide it” had no anchored sentence: 2242 and 2243 answer only “must they refuse”, and the paragraph that answers the other is 2471 — “in situations that require witness to the faith, the Christian must profess it without equivocation”. Added 2026-09-10 with 2472 and 2473, the latter being _martyrdom_, a keyword that had nothing behind it either. 2471–2473 now open the page and 2242–2243 follow, which is the order the question asks them in.

civitas-catholica.note: Was C, and the missing paragraphs were the ones this reader arrives quoting: 2105 states “the traditional Catholic teaching on the moral duty of individuals and societies toward the true religion and the one Church of Christ”, and 2107 states what follows if a state does give one religious community special civil recognition — the religious freedom of all must still be recognized. Both were on `libertas-religiosa` and neither was here. Added 2026-09-10. 2245 was already carrying the other side: the Church “is not to be confused in any way with the political community”.

libertas-religiosa.note: 2106 answers both halves of the question in one sentence, and 2108 meets _error has no rights_ head-on: religious liberty is “neither a moral license to adhere to error, nor a supposed right to error, but rather a natural right of the human person to civil liberty”. 2109 then says the right is not unlimited, which keeps the page from reading as a concession. 2105–2107 are shared with `civitas-catholica`, which asks the opposite question of the same paragraphs.

oecologia.note: Was C on _creation_: three of the four anchored paragraphs were about animals — kindness to them, experimentation on them, not spending on them what the poor need — and a reader asking why any of this is the Church’s business got St Philip Neri. The reason is at 339, which was on no topic: each creature “reflects in its own way a ray of God’s infinite wisdom”, and disordered use of things “would bring disastrous consequences for human beings and their environment”, written in 1992. Added 2026-09-10 with 344, the Canticle of the Creatures. _Climate change_ and _global warming_ have no Catechism text and are not going to; the Compendium block and _laudato-si_ carry them.

paupertas.note: Asked what is required of those who have enough, 2446 answers with Chrysostom and not with a principle — “not to enable the poor to share in our goods is to steal from them and deprive them of life” — and adds that what is due in justice “is not to be offered as a gift of charity”, which is the sentence a reader who thinks of this as charity needs. 2447 lists the works of mercy, so _almsgiving_, _homeless_ and _hunger_ all have text.

technologia.note: 2294 is the sentence that transfers — “it is an illusion to claim moral neutrality in scientific research and its applications” — and CSDC 460 is the one for _transhumanism_: man “sets himself up in place of God”. B because neither work is addressed to machines that think and neither could be, the Catechism being 1992 and the Compendium 2004; _antiqua-et-nova_ (2025) is the only text in the corpus that is, and a document can only be named. Was diluted: CSDC 458–459 is agriculture, molecular biology and genetic manipulation of plants, which is a different technology question and mostly `oecologia`’s. Narrowed 2026-09-10.

communicatio-socialis.note: 2494 states the right — society’s right to information “based on truth, freedom, justice and solidarity” — 2497 puts the duty on journalists by name, 2498 on civil authorities, and 2499 on states that falsify systematically, so _propaganda_, _censorship_ and _fake news_ each have a paragraph. 2496 is the one addressed to the reader rather than to the press, and it is why the page is not only about other people.

iudaismus.note: 839 is the answer and it is unambiguous — “the gifts and the call of God are irrevocable”, and the Jewish faith “unlike other non-Christian religions, is already a response to God’s revelation”. Was C on _deicide_ and _antisemitism_, keywords with no anchored sentence anywhere in the file. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 597, which says neither the Jews of Jerusalem as a whole nor Jews of other times can be charged, quoting the Council directly, and 598, which turns it round: the Church “does not hesitate to impute to Christians the gravest responsibility for the torments inflicted upon Jesus, a responsibility with which they have all too often burdened the Jews alone”. A page on this question that omits 597 is a page that leaves the accusation standing.

islam.note: 841 is the whole of what the Catechism says about Muslims, and it answers _same god_ in its own words: “together with us they adore the one, merciful God”. 843 was added beside it — the Church recognizes in other religions “that search, among shadows and images, for the God who is unknown yet near” — because one paragraph was the entire page, and 843 is the stance the reader is asking about even though it is general. _Quran_, _mohammed_ and _sharia_ have no text in any work this site quotes; _nostra-aetate_ is where they are.

salus-extra-ecclesiam.note: 846 states the hard sentence and 847 immediately says whom it is not aimed at, which is the pair a reader asking about everyone who is not Catholic needs to meet in that order. Was C on _baptism of desire_, a keyword with no anchored sentence; 1258–1260 added 2026-09-10 — baptism of blood, the catechumen who dies before baptism, and every man ignorant of the Gospel who seeks the truth and does God’s will as he understands it. Shared with `infans-non-baptizatus`, which needs them for one particular grief.

proselytismus.note: 849 gives the mandate, 851 the motive, and 856 the manner — “a respectful dialogue with those who do not yet accept the Gospel”, in which believers “can profit … by learning to appreciate better those elements of truth and grace which are found among peoples”. 853 is why the run is taken whole: it is the Church admitting the “discrepancy existing between the message she proclaims and the human weakness of those to whom the Gospel has been entrusted”, which is the reader’s objection stated before they make it.

note: Was C: the question is whether a convert must give up the customs they were raised in, and the anchor was 1200–1206 on the liturgical rites of the Church — Ambrosian, Byzantine, Coptic, Maronite — which is a catalogue and not an answer. Re-anchored 2026-09-10 on 843, goodness and truth in other religions as “a preparation for the Gospel”; 854, the only paragraph that uses the word — mission “must involve a process of inculturation if the Gospel is to take flesh in each people’s culture”; and 1204–1206, where cultures are “not abolished by it, but redeemed and fulfilled”, some parts may be adapted and some may not, and adaptation “requires a conversion of heart”. That last clause is why _syncretism_ needs no separate paragraph.

polygamia.note: 2387 opens on the reader’s own predicament — a man “obliged to repudiate one or more wives with whom he has shared years of conjugal life” — and ends on the grave duty in justice toward them. Was C on _pauline privilege_, and on the question’s own words: what BECOMES of the other wives is a procedure, and procedures are the Code’s. Added 2026-09-10: can. 1148, which lets a man who receives baptism retain one wife “if it is hard for him to remain with the first one” and tells the local ordinary to keep the moral, social and economic conditions of the place in view.

superstitio.note: 2111 answers the question by drawing the line inside religion rather than outside it: superstition “can affect the worship we offer the true God”, when one attributes efficacy to prayers or sacramental signs “in their mere external performance”. Was C on _charms_, _spells_, _witchcraft_ and _blessing away an illness_, none of which had a sentence. Added 2026-09-10: 2117, which names charms, sorcery “even if this were for the sake of restoring their health”, and “so-called traditional cures”. Only 2117 and not 2115–2117: horoscopes and mediums are `divinatio`, and taking the run whole made that topic a strict subset of this one, which is the state the file’s own rule exists to prevent.

evangelium-prosperitatis.note: The anchors contradict the premise rather than answering the question: 2544 says the precept of detachment from riches “is obligatory for entrance into the Kingdom of heaven” and 2547 that the Lord “grieves over the rich, because they find their consolation in the abundance of goods”. A reader asking whether God rewards faith with money has to draw the conclusion themselves, which is what B means. Nothing in the corpus’s quotable works names prosperity preaching; _evangelii-gaudium_ on the idolatry of money is the nearest and is already listed.

aegritudo.note: CCC 1500–1513 is the Anointing article's own four headings whole, and 1505 and 1508 say the thing the reader needs — _he did not heal all the sick_, and _my grace is sufficient for you_.

finis-vitae.note: 2278 answers "must every treatment be continued" in its first clause and names who decides. Inside `euthanasia`, correctly: this reader is a family at a bedside, not an argument.

post-mortem.note: `lead` 1032 answers the second half of the question, prayer for the dead. can. 1176 added 2026-09-10 for _funeral, wake, burial_; its §2 is written about the living. Keywords reach into grief.

infans-non-baptizatus.note: `lead` 1261 is the whole topic — _allow us to hope that there is a way of salvation_. can. 1183 added 2026-09-10 for the _stillborn_ and _miscarried_ keywords: a funeral can be permitted.

mors-voluntaria.note: See the duplicate note below. can. 1176 and 1184 added 2026-09-10: funerals are owed to the faithful, and the list of those deprived of them does not include suicide.

crematio.note: "May a Catholic be cremated" is 2301; "and may the ashes be scattered" is in _Ad resurgendum cum Christo_, which the page names and does not quote. No quotable work in the corpus answers it.

matrimonium.note: CCC 1626 and can. 1057 both say consent makes the marriage, which is the question's own words. Was short one keyword: _convalidation_ had no text, fixed 2026-09-10 with can. 1156–1160 taken as the chapter. _banns_ still promises nothing.

matrimonium-mixtum.note: CCC 1633–1637 is the Catechism's own heading whole, and can. 1125 answers the second half of the question — _and of which of us_ — by listing promises the Catholic party makes and the other party is only told about.

infidelitas-coniugis.note: `lead` 1649 opens on the Church permitting physical separation, and can. 1152 states the right in law. The keywords reach into `divortium` and `nullitas-matrimonii`; both exist, so the search returns all three rather than the wrong one.

nullitas-matrimonii.note: Was C: "Am I still married?" was answered with venue rules — which tribunal is competent — and never with the grounds, though _defect of consent_ is a keyword. Fixed 2026-09-10 with can. 1095 and 1103.

communio-post-divortium.note: Was C and a strict subset of `nullitas-matrimonii`: two shared paragraphs and nothing of its own. Fixed 2026-09-10 with CCC 1385, the general rule 1650 applies, and can. 915–916, where the reader can see they are not the excommunicated case.

graviditas.note: Was C, and the worst door mismatch found: a page titled _Pregnancy and miscarriage_ whose second paragraph called abortion an abominable crime. 2271 dropped and 1261 added 2026-09-10.

sterilitas.note: `lead` 2379 is "what is left to us" in the Catechism's own words, down to adoption. `fecundatio-artificialis` sits inside it, which is the documented pair.

adoptio.note: can. 110 answers "is the child ours in the Church's eyes" verbatim, and can. 1094 covers the keyword nobody expects to need.

educatio-filiorum.note: Was C: every anchor was the parents' duty to teach, and the question is what to do when the child refuses. 2217 and 2230 added 2026-09-10 — the child at home, and the adult who chooses.

filius-a-fide-lapsus.note: Was C: "Where did we go wrong?" was answered with eleven paragraphs on what parents owe, which reads as the indictment. CCC 1730–1732 added 2026-09-10 — _man is the father of his acts_.

parentes.note: Was C: nothing met _abusive mother_ or _cut them off_. 2232 added 2026-09-10 — _family ties are important but not absolute_ — though its own context is vocation. No paragraph addresses an abusive parent.

cura-parentum.note: "I cannot do it all" is answered by three words inside 2218, _as much as they can_. Nothing in the corpus is about the carer; CSDC 222 is about valuing the elderly. Adjacent to the blocklist.

amissio-operis.note: `lead` 2436 is the Catechism saying unemployment wounds its victim's dignity; CSDC 287 calls it a real social disaster.

pornographia.note: Was C: three paragraphs of definition and nothing on "not being able to stop", while the keywords opened on _addiction_. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 2342 (self-mastery is never acquired once and for all) and 1735.

masturbatio.note: CCC 2352's closing sentence answers "is it always a mortal sin" in the Catechism's own words, and 1735 generalises it.

homosexualitas-vivenda.note: 2358–2359 is a what-do-I-do text rather than a teaching, which is the whole reason it is a separate topic from `homosexualitas`, which keeps 2357.

post-contraceptionem.note: Was C twice over: no anchored text said the word _sterilisation_, and "what now?" was answered only by 2370, which is `contraceptio`'s own teaching restated. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 2399 and 1451–1453.

adulterium.note: "Do I have to tell?" is answered only by 2487, which is written about offences against truth and reputation and reaches a spouse by analogy — correctly, since it says reparation is owed and may be made secretly. Checked: no better paragraph.

remissio-peccatorum.note: Was C: CCC 982 answers "too grave to be forgiven" in its first line, and the keyword _sin against the holy spirit_ had nothing at all. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 1864, which quotes Mt 12:31 and then says what the refusal actually is.

reditus.note: Was C, and a strict subset of `scrupulositas` besides: 1455–1458 is what confession requires, including the annual obligation this reader has not kept. Fixed 2026-09-10 with 1439 (the prodigal son, the journey back, the welcome) and 1465 to close.

scrupulositas.note: Was C by ordering alone: the page opened on 1454, _prepare by an examination of conscience_, which is the one thing this reader cannot stop doing. `lead` 1456 now opens on the answer — _strive to confess all the sins that they can remember_ — 2026-09-10.

post-abortum.note: Was C: 2272 named the excommunication and nothing said it could be lifted. Fixed 2026-09-10 with CCC 1463 and the topic's first canon, 1357, where a confessor may remit it in the internal forum.

venia-danda.note: "Do I have to?" is answered inside 2843 — _it is not in our power not to feel or to forget an offense_ — after that paragraph's own opening on the merciless servant. No ordering surfaces it without splitting a paragraph, which the file forbids.

mortis-desiderium.note: `lead` 2283 puts _we should not despair of the eternal salvation of persons who have taken their own lives_ first, which is the question verbatim, and 2282 closes on diminished responsibility. See the keyword note below.

dubium-fidei.note: Was C: nothing anchored said faith is ever dark. Fixed 2026-09-10 by widening 162 to the Catechism's own 162–165 and adding 2731 on dryness.

amor-dei.note: Was C: 218–221 is God's love for **Israel**, and the reader's whole objection is that it applies to everyone but them. Fixed 2026-09-10 with CCC 604–605 anchored ahead of it, which also retired the `lead`.

oratio-inaudita.note: CCC 2734–2741 is the Catechism's own two headings on this exact question, taken whole and unreordered — the ideal case, where the topic is barely editorial. 2737 lands hard on a reader whose petition was for a dying child; excising it would be choosing by hand.

divinatio.note: 2116 lists horoscopes, palm reading, clairvoyance and mediums by name, which is "what is actually forbidden" answered in the Catechism's own inventory.

signa.note: It gives the posture — trust providence, do not demand proof — and never adjudicates a particular event, which is the honest answer. _Opened the bible at random_ is 2116's.

mortui.note: Nothing says the dead do not return; 1022 added 2026-09-10 so the reader can at least see they are already judged, and 2116 forbids summoning them. The inference is theirs.

daemones.note: Was C by ordering: "Does the Church still do that?" was answered in the seventh paragraph. `lead` 1673 set 2026-09-10.

angeli.note: Was C by ordering: the guardian angel is 336, last of nine. `lead` 336 set 2026-09-10.

apparitiones.note: Two paragraphs, and 67 answers "does a Catholic have to believe" outright. Nothing on how an apparition is approved; the corpus has no text.

miracula-et-reliquiae.note: CCC 1674 is the only paragraph in the Catechism that says "relics", and it says it in a list. 828 added 2026-09-10 for _canonisation_. Nothing on incorrupt bodies.

experientia-mortis-proximae.note: 1021–1022 gives the framework — judgment at the moment of death — and the corpus says nothing about near-death experiences. The reader carries it across or nothing does.

finis-mundi.note: 675–676 is the Antichrist and the rejection of millenarianism, which is exactly what _rapture_ and _three days of darkness_ are owed.

oratio.note: Was C: the Catechism gives three expressions of prayer and the topic carried two, while _contemplation_ and _mental prayer_ were keywords. 2709–2712 added 2026-09-10.

ieiunium.note: can. 1251 and 1252 are the days and the ages, which is the question exactly. can. 919 added 2026-09-10 for the eucharistic fast, a keyword with no text behind it.

dominica.note: 2181 names the grave sin and the excusing reasons in one paragraph, and 2183 covers the case where Mass is impossible.

otium.note: 2185's _the charity of truth seeks holy leisure_ and CSDC 284's _rest from work is a right_ answer a reader who suspects doing nothing is a fault.

initiatio-adultorum.note: 1232 names the RCIA and can. 851 and 865 say what the catechumenate asks. _Baptised as a baby, never confirmed_ is a different path and only 1231 glances at it.

baptismus-infantium.note: can. 874 is the godparent question answered as a checklist, and 1255 says what is asked of them. See the Latin clause noted below.

organorum-donatio.note: 2296 answers both halves of the question in one paragraph, in life and after death, including consent.

corpus-ornandum.note: The Catechism does not contain the word "tattoo" or "piercing"; 2289 gives the principle against the cult of the body. 2290 added 2026-09-10 for _gym_ and _dieting_.

decimae.note: The answer is that there is no number — _each according to his abilities_ — which is what a reader holding the word _tithe_ most needs to be told.

vota-et-iuramenta.note: 2102 defines a vow verbatim and 2103 closes on dispensation, which is the keyword a reader who has broken one arrives with.

vocatio.note: Was C and the clearest case of a title read as an oracle: CCC 1877–1889 says "vocation" and means subsidiarity and socialisation. Replaced 2026-09-10 with 2013–2016, 1533–1535, 898–900 and 2233.

merces-iusta.note: 2434 says what a wage is supposed to cover, at the length of the question, and CSDC 304 covers the strike the title also promises.

pecunia-collocanda.note: Was C: the topic is titled _Investing and speculation_ and the paragraph naming speculation, 2409, was on the tax page. 2409 and 2413 (games of chance) added 2026-09-10.

tributum.note: 2240 makes paying taxes morally obligatory in its first line, which answers "is cheating on it a sin" without needing a second paragraph.

invidia.note: 2539 names the sadness at another's goods and 2540 gives the remedy: _rejoice in your brother's progress_.

acedia.note: 2094 and 2733 both name acedia, and 2733's _a form of depression due to lax ascetical practice_ is the sentence. _Spiritual dryness_ is 2731 and belongs to prayer, which is the distinction worth making.

discrimen-gentium.note: 1935 names race. Was diluted: CSDC 146–147 is male and female complementarity and 148 is disability, neither of which is racism; narrowed to 144–145 on 2026-09-10.

mercatura-hominum.note: 2414 forbids human beings "being bought, sold and exchanged like merchandise", which is the question in the Catechism's own words.

violentia-domestica.note: Was C and the most consequential: one paragraph, about rape, and nothing telling a reader being beaten that they may leave. CCC 1649 and can. 1153–1154 added 2026-09-10.

violentia-digitalis.note: Was C: privacy was anchored at 2488–2492 and reputation, which the title promises, was not. 2477–2479 added 2026-09-10 — detraction and calumny, which is what _gossip_ and _cancelling_ are.

debilitas.note: 2276 uses the title's own word and CSDC 148 develops it. 2274 added 2026-09-10 for _prenatal screening_, which is how most readers arrive at this page.

carceres.note: CSDC 402–404 answers what may be done to an offender, and 405 states the death-penalty teaching as it stood before CCC 2267 was revised in 2018. Both are kept: choosing between two magisterial texts is not this file’s to do. B because the reader is shown the older position with nothing on the page saying when either was written — see the open question in docs/research/topic-anchor-review.md.

defensio-sui.note: 2264 answers "how far" with the moderation test. Was diluted: 2317 and CSDC 500–501 are states at war, which is `bellum`, and were dropped 2026-09-10.

proles-suscipienda.note: CSDC 232 carries the phrase the reader needs — _to avoid for a time or even indeterminately a new birth_ — beside 2368's warning against selfishness.
